Stack the cohort at each step into one data frame

Source: R/characteristics.R
stack_cohorts.Rd

Returns the rows of the cohort surviving each step (or, with excluded = TRUE, the rows removed at each step), stacked with a step factor and a step_number column in front of the original columns. A row that survives several steps appears once per step. This is the input shape summary-table packages expect, e.g. gtsummary::tbl_summary(stack_cohorts(flow), by = step, include = c(age, sex)); as_characteristics_tibble() is the dependency-light equivalent.

Usage

stack_cohorts(
  flow,
  steps = NULL,
  excluded = FALSE,
  level = NULL,
  drop_randomise = TRUE,
  assessed_label = "Assessed for eligibility"
)

Arguments

flow

A cf_flow object produced by apply_criteria().

steps

Optional step selectors (a vector or list); see the section "Steps". NULL (default) means every step.

excluded

Logical. FALSE (default) describes the cohort surviving each step; TRUE describes the rows removed at each step.

level

Optional hierarchy level name at which to count units; see the section "Hierarchy levels". Requires a flow built with a hierarchy.

drop_randomise

Logical. Omit randomise() steps when steps is NULL (default TRUE).

assessed_label

Heading for step 0, the starting data. Default "Assessed for eligibility".

Value

A tibble: step_number (integer), step (factor whose levels are the step headings in column order), then the data columns. With level, only the level's key column(s) and the columns constant within every unit of that level are kept.

Steps

By default there is one column per step from 0 (the starting data) to the last step, omitting randomise() steps (see drop_randomise). Column k holds cohort(flow, step_number = k): the rows that passed steps 1 to k. steps restricts or reorders the columns. Each element is resolved like at in cohort(): a number is a step number (0 = starting data); a string is a step label if one matches, else a category, meaning its last step. Steps named in steps are never dropped, even randomise() steps.

With excluded = TRUE, column k instead holds the rows removed at step k (those of excluded() with cf_step == k): the usual supplementary table of excluded participants' characteristics. Step 0 removes nothing and cannot be selected.

A column's heading is the step label, or assessed_label for step 0. Repeated headings are made unique with " #<n>".

Hierarchy levels

When the flow was built with apply_criteria(hierarchy = ), rows are summarised unless level names one of the hierarchy's levels, in which case each unit at that level (each distinct, complete key) contributes once and n counts units. A row with an NA in the level's key is not a unit. Every variable must then be constant within each unit across the starting data; a variable that varies within a unit is an error, since there is no single value to summarise.

See also

as_characteristics_tibble(), cohort(), excluded().

Other flow accessors: cohort(), criteria_status(), excluded()

Examples

dat  <- mock_parallel_rct(n_participants = 200, seed = 1)
crit <- cf_criteria() |>
  include(~ age >= 18, label = "Adults only") |>
  include(~ eligible_screen, label = "Passed screening") |>
  exclude(~ withdrew, label = "Withdrew consent")
flow <- apply_criteria(dat, crit, id = "participant_id")
stacked <- stack_cohorts(flow)
table(stacked$step)
#> 
#> Assessed for eligibility              Adults only         Passed screening 
#>                      200                      184                      169 
#>         Withdrew consent 
#>                      162
